text:
A rideshare dropped adult newcomer Mara with one suitcase at Fulcrum's
redwood-and-glass compound on a curving Northern California coast
before evening. A tall man in a black suit stepped out from under
a red-and-white striped awning to carry the suitcase. "I'm Adrian,
the Head of Fulcrum," he said with an unforced smile. "Welcome." Mara
uncomfortably noticed how he held open a glass door with his body
rather than one hand.

Adrian led Mara in, past a row of small potted palms and a stone
waterfall to the right, under a painting of a waterfall. A young man
in a black suit walked out from the center doors ahead of them. He
spotted Mara. "Ah! You're here! Welcome." He stopped at the outer door
and Adrian passed him with a slight incline of his head. They entered
a double-height space with a skylight and potted palms between
the reception area, a long table with white chairs and white cloths,
and two short black couches. The other young man in a black suit led
Mara to a short couch facing a potted palm in a rough stone pot. "Wait
here please," Adrian said before leaving Mara to sit in silence for a
few minutes.

The sound of the stone waterfall became louder and more distinct.
Mara relaxed slightly. Another younger man appeared and offered a tray
of flutes full of golden liquid, a small stack of folded white napkins,
and a small platter of tiny savory treats. "Welcome to Fulcrum,"
the young man said brightly. Mara picked up a flute and took a sip,
noticing how smoothly the effervescent liquid slid down her throat.
The young man placed two other flutes with golden liquid on a low table
adjacent to where Mara sat, then disappeared behind the reception
counter. Mara tasted one of the tiny savory treats, noticing that it
was warm, not hot.

Adrian reappeared in a few minutes. He pulled up a chair and sat down,
placing his flute on the table between them. The young man at the
reception area reappeared and silently placed another flute with golden
liquid on the table near Adrian. He returned to the reception area.

"Welcome," Adrian said with an unforced smile. "I'm Adrian, the Head
of Fulcrum." Mara looked at the flutes in front of Adrian. She smiled
and nodded. "Mara," she said. "Thank you." Adrian raised his flute
slightly, and Mara raised her flute to match. They both drank.

A rideshare left adult newcomer Mara with one suitcase at Fulcrum's redwood-and-glass Northern California compound before an evening welcome. A man and woman greeted her, handed off her suitcase, and walked her toward a low building where she recognized Adrian's voice from the video messages she had watched while applying for a six-week intensive. The voice seemed both loud and distant at first, then settled into a pleasant rumble that made sense with the face of the bearded man standing next to two people who were talking about a conversation.

Mara waved off the man and woman who had met her and introduced herself to Adrian, who shook her hand, nodded to the others, and walked toward the far end of the building. She followed without catching any conversation as she passed people she was hearing and seeing for the first time. The others scattered in different directions while she stuck near Adrian, whose voice seemed louder in her presence.

He mentioned the food waiting and said she would meet people for dinner at the welcome, so there was no hurry. She smiled and looked around as he spoke about the area around them. They passed several low buildings that looked like they contained dorms, and she wondered where to look for hers. Adrian pointed out two structures that were farther away. She recognized them from the videos.

Adrian stopped to introduce Mara to a couple of people who were sitting on a couch outside the structure that he said contained dorms. The couple looked sleepy, but smiled and shook her hand. Adrian continued toward a wide outdoor dining area. He described some activities that would take place there over the next few weeks and asked Mara if she had any questions about the food, which seemed to be his focus. She asked if there was vegetarian or vegan food.

He answered yes and added that they had tried hard to offer options for different dietary requirements. She realized this might have been true when she first visited Fulcrum a year ago, but it had changed now that Fulcrum was an official institute. She wondered how many people there were in the room that Adrian had pointed out as the welcome location. It seemed huge even from the distance that they were, and she could tell that Adrian had already noticed the lights over there, which had turned on within a minute of their arrival.

In the rideshare from SFO, Mara made small talk with the driver. "Have you taken many guests to Fulcrum? Any tips?"

The driver, who had been distracted, turned a surprised look back at her. "Oh, that place! My partner went on retreat there recently. I'm taking him back after this run."

"Really? What was it like?" Mara felt an involuntary frisson of anxiety. She'd been chosen as one of the few who would be accepted that week, but she still wasn't sure what to expect.

"Well, it's a little strange at first," the driver said, with an amused glance in the rearview mirror. "Like some kind of secret society, you know?" He nodded to a side road that led toward Fulcrum. "You can tell by the way they don't show up on Google Maps."

Mara laughed nervously, but her curiosity was piqued. The driver continued, "The way they talk about things can be a bit...abstract. They seem to focus on these invisible rules that everyone knows but can't really explain."

Mara nodded slowly, absorbing this. "So what did you think of the place when you dropped him off?"

"Oh, it looked fine enough," the driver replied, shrugging. "Kind of upscale, you know? Like a fancy retreat center or something. But there was something about the way people interacted there, like they were all on a different wavelength."

Mara leaned forward, intrigued. "What do you mean?"

The driver looked back at her again, his expression thoughtful. "Like there's an invisible code that everyone understands except you. Like being dropped into the middle of a private joke, and you're the only one who doesn't get it." He chuckled. "My partner came back all full of new jargon, but he wasn't much help explaining any of it."

They continued in silence for a moment before the driver turned back to Mara with an apologetic smile. "Sorry if I'm making it sound too weird. They say my partner really got a lot out of the experience. He seemed happier, you know? But it does take some getting used to."

In my rideshare on the way up from San Francisco, the driver and I
discussed whether Fulcrum was a cult or not. He said he was looking for
a girlfriend, and that some women might be vulnerable to cult influence.

“What is your opinion?” I asked him.

“I think you should be careful,” he said.

When he pulled to the end of the paved drive at the Fulcrum compound,
it was just after 6 PM and a little too dark for my eyes to adjust and
see the whole thing at once. I had a little trouble finding the entrance
in the dim light. A group of people were gathered around the front
doors. One of them stepped forward and waved me over. “Hello,” I said.
“Are you Mara?” she asked, then opened the front doors for me. “I’m
Gladys.” We shook hands.

“Welcome to Fulcrum,” she said.

She turned out not to be Gladys, who was a younger woman with very
short hair. The taller woman who greeted me instead was a senior staff
member of the organization.

She took my bags and showed me to my room, and then told me there’s a
group dinner tonight. She said that if I’d like to join, I should go to
the main dining area now. “We start at 6:30 PM sharp,” she said.

I asked where that was.

She said she would take me there. We walked through the main building,
and then outside a bit and down some stairs.

“Oh yes, here we are, welcome to our dining area,” she said.

A lot of people were already standing around, mostly young, some older.
They all seemed very relaxed. I knew it was a nice dinner because I
could smell it; there was a large buffet table laid out with food. Some
of the people were serving themselves and sitting at tables.

“Let me introduce you,” she said. “My name is Jane.” She brought me over
to some of the other new people like me, and we all chatted about where
we came from and why we were here. One guy asked if this was a cult.

“So far not yet,” I said. “It seems friendly.”

Everyone laughed. We had all just come to work here. Some of us would be
doing research, but I was going to be doing administrative things. A
woman named Mary would be showing me where everything is tomorrow.
